equipment_and_construction_summary.title: Domains at War: Campaigns - Equipment and Construction

item.name: Helmet, Light
item.cost: included in armor; 5gp if purchased separately

item.name: Archery Target
item.rule: Training device for marksmanship.
Cost is already included in missile troop training costs.

item.name: Army Emblem
item.rule: Mounted above an army standard.
If an army standard has no emblem, the army's morale score is reduced by 1.
Loss of an army standard and/or emblem reduces morale by 1 and counts as a calamity.

item.name: Barding
item.rule: Large barding uses the horse barding type as the base reference.
Huge barding costs and weighs 3 times horse barding of the same type.
Gigantic barding costs and weighs 12 times horse barding of the same type.
Colossal barding costs and weighs 60 times horse barding of the same type.

shared_rules.rule: Each chariot has three built-in weapon cases holding a composite bow, 3 javelins, and 20 arrows.
Movement through desert, forest, mountain, or swamp requires a road.

item.name: Craftsman's Tools
item.rule: Required to make Craft proficiency throws.
Each craft requires its own specific tools.

item.name: Craftsman's Workshop
item.rule: Contains enough tools and furnishings for up to 8 craftsmen to work together.
A master craftsman must have access to a workshop to increase the productivity of journeymen and apprentices.
Each craft requires its own specific workshop.

item.name: Crutch
item.rule: Used by characters with missing or maimed legs who lack prostheses.

item.name: Earplugs
item.rule: Protect the wearer from loud sounds.

item.name: Flag
item.rule: Pennants identify company-sized units or individual heroes.
Banners identify battalion- or regiment-sized units.
Standards identify brigade-sized units, divisions, and armies.
Standards may be topped by army emblems.
If a unit or division lacks a flag of the appropriate size, its morale score is reduced by 1.
Loss of a unit's flag reduces morale by 1 and counts as a calamity.

row.use: company-sized unit or individual hero insignia

item.name: Helmet, Heavy
item.rule: Must be purchased separately from armor.
Imposes -1 to surprise rolls.
Imposes -4 to proficiency throws to hear noise.
Grants +2 on d20 rolls on the Mortal Wounds table.

item.name: Helmet, Light
item.rule: Included in the cost of any suit of armor.
If armor is worn without a helmet, decrease armor class by 1 point.
If purchased separately for 5gp, it provides no in-game benefit.

item.name: Howdah
item.rule: May be built for riding or war.
War howdahs cost and weigh twice as much as riding howdahs.

row.war_occupant_bonus: +3 AC and +3 saves vs Blast from artillery, burning oil, or similar effects
+4 AC and +4 saves vs Blast from artillery, burning oil, or similar effects
+4 AC and +4 saves vs Blast from artillery, burning oil, or similar effects

item.name: Laborers' Tools
item.rule: Required for troops assisting on construction projects.

item.name: Musical Instrument, Military
item.rule: Used to call to arms, issue orders, call to quarters, and signal commands.

item.name: Pell
item.rule: Training device for infantry sword-and-shield practice.
Cost is already included in infantry training costs.

item.name: Prosthesis
item.rule: Basic prostheses are made of wood or bronze.
Iron prostheses cost x2; silver x5; gold x50.
A prosthetic arm or hand restores ability to use a shield.
A prosthetic arm or hand may instead be replaced with a weapon such as a club, hook, or short sword.
A prosthetic leg or foot allows walking without a crutch but does not remove movement or Dexterity penalties from limb loss.

item.name: Quintain
item.rule: Training device for cavalry lance-and-sword practice.
Cost is already included in cavalry training costs.

item.name: Shield, Mirrored
item.rule: May be used as a mirror when fighting a monster with a gaze attack to reduce penalties from averting one's gaze.
A monster with a petrifying gaze that attacks a character wielding a mirror shield has a 1-2 on 1d6 chance of seeing its own reflection unless it averts its own eyes.

item.name: Surgical Saw
item.rule: Used for amputations when healing mortally, grievously, or critically wounded characters suffering from permanent wounds.
Small saw grants +2 on Healing proficiency throws for this use.
Large saw grants +4 on Healing proficiency throws for this use.

item.name: Whistle
item.rule: Emits a shrill sound audible at great distance.

artillery_characteristics_rules.rule: Artillery are siege weapons designed to bombard and destroy enemy ships and structures.
AC is the armor class of the artillery piece.
SHP is the structural hit points of the artillery piece.
Artillery is most effective with the listed ammunition weight.
If firing lighter or heavier ammunition than designated, reduce maximum range by 25%.
Artillery cannot attack targets closer than minimum range or farther than maximum range.
Against ships or structures, a successful hit deals SHP damage to the target and listed area damage to creatures in the area of effect.
Against creatures, a successful hit deals damage to the struck creature and the listed area of effect.
Creatures in the area of effect may save vs Blast to avoid or reduce damage as applicable; the direct target cannot avoid damage from the direct hit.
If the modified artillery attack throw, ignoring the creature's AC, would have hit, a miss still lands near enough to affect the creature as part of the area of effect.
Pitch ammunition deals fire damage to ships and wooden structures each turn until extinguished.
Pitch ammunition deals fire damage to creatures each round while they remain in the area or until the fire is extinguished.
Five creatures extinguish a fire in 3 turns; each additional five creatures reduces the time by 1 turn to a minimum of 1 turn.
Artillery attacks as the lowest-level crew member.
Crews without an artillerist suffer -4 to attack throws.
Crude ammunition imposes -2 to attack throws.
Crews without an artillerist specialist halve their rate of fire.

type.name: Ballista
type.rule: Light ballista can damage creatures only; they cannot damage structures.
Medium ballista can damage creatures and wooden structures, but cannot damage stone.
Heavy ballista can damage creatures, wood, and stone.

type.name: Ballista, Repeating
type.rule: On an unmodified attack throw of 1, the weapon malfunctions.
A siege engineer requires 1 turn to repair a malfunction; the weapon cannot fire during repair.

type.name: Catapult
type.rule: All catapults can damage creatures, wood, and stone.
Catapults suffer -4 to attack throws against man-sized creatures.
Catapults suffer -2 to attack throws against large creatures.
Catapults suffer an additional -1 to attack throws per 10' of movement the creature moved.

type.name: Trebuchet
type.rule: Trebuchets share catapult targeting benefits and drawbacks against creatures and structures.
Counterweight trebuchets gain +2 to attack throws.

item.name: Battering Ram
item.rule: Typical size is 20' long, 2' diameter, 4,000lb.
Larger rams cost 10gp per foot.
Requires 5 man-sized crew per 5' of ram.
Moves 30' per round by crew, or may be mounted in a movable gallery.
May batter once every other round once adjacent to a structure.
Each blow deals 4d10 SHP to wooden structures and 1d4 SHP to stone structures.
A 20' ram has AC 2 and 4 SHP, or 1 SHP per 5'.
For variant dimensions, adjust price, SHP, and damage proportionately.

item.name: Cauldron, Suspended
item.rule: Affects a 10' radius area or all creatures on a siege ladder.
Deals 1d8 damage per round for 2 rounds.
Save vs Blast reduces damage to 1d3.

item.name: Fascine
item.rule: Purchased in 10' x 10' x 10' cubes.
Used to reinforce fortifications, fill moats, or cross wet terrain.

item.name: Hoist
item.rule: Transports up to 4 man-sized creatures in a basket.
Basket ascends or descends in 1 round.
Resetting the counterweight takes 4 rounds between ascents.
Ascending creatures gain partial cover; missile attacks against them suffer -2.
Can be mounted in movable galleries or siege towers.
Hoist has AC 0 and 5-10 SHP.

item.name: Movable Gallery
item.rule: Provides cover for troops operating against a wall.
Missile attacks against creatures inside suffer -4.
Occupants gain +4 to saves vs Blast from artillery, burning oil, or similar effects.
Typical size is 12' tall, 12' wide, 20' long; protects 20 man-sized creatures.
Gallery has AC 1 and 10 SHP.
Can mount a battering ram, hoist, or screw purchased separately.
Moves 30' per round if occupied by at least 10 man-sized creatures.
Larger galleries cost 1gp per square foot.

item.name: Movable Mantlet
item.rule: Missile attacks against creatures protected by the mantlet suffer -4.
Protected creatures gain +4 to saves vs Blast from artillery, burning oil, or similar effects.
Typical size is 8' by 6' and protects 2 man-sized creatures.
Mantlet has AC 1 and 2 SHP.
Shield includes slits allowing archery fire.

item.name: Petard

procedure.step: Lighting the fuse requires a Siege Engineering proficiency throw of 6+.
On success, the petard detonates in 1d4 rounds.
On failure, the fuse is not lit.
On an unmodified 1, the petard fumbles and detonates immediately.

item.rule: Creatures may save vs Blast for half damage.
Petards deal full damage to SHP of ships and buildings.

procedure.step: Make an attack throw against the ram at -4.
If hit, the ram saves vs Paralysis using the lowest level member of its crew.
On failed save, the ram is dislodged and takes 1d6 SHP damage.

item.name: Screw
item.rule: Typical size is 20' long.
Larger screws cost 10gp per foot.
Requires 2-5 man-sized crew per 5'.
Moves 30' per round by crew, or may be mounted in a movable gallery.
May bore once every other round once adjacent to a structure.
Each bore deals 3d10 SHP to wooden structures and 1d4+1 SHP to stone structures.
A 20' screw has AC 2 and 4 SHP, or 1 SHP per 5'.
For variant dimensions, adjust price, SHP, and damage proportionately.

procedure.step: Make an attack throw against the target creature at -4, also applying any cover modifier.
If hit, the target saves vs Paralysis.
On failed save, the target is knocked off the wall and takes falling damage of 1d6 per 10'.

item.name: Siege Ladder
item.rule: Creatures climb at 1/4 normal movement rate.
A defender may push a ladder away with a successful proficiency throw to open doors.
Each man-sized creature on the ladder applies a -1 penalty to that throw.

shared_rules.rule: Missile attacks against creatures inside the tower suffer -4.
Occupants gain +4 to saves vs Blast from artillery, burning oil, or similar effects.
If properly crewed, a siege tower moves 30' per round.
External crew may be replaced by draft animals or exotic creatures at 1 external crew per 10 stone of normal load.

equipment_availability_on_campaign.rule: An army of 1,200 troops (12 units) or more functions as its own market for equipment availability.
This benefit is lost if supply lines are blocked or over-extended.

civilian_structures_table.rule: Dimensions marked in the source as alterable may be changed so long as square footage remains the same.

structure_characteristics.rule: When a structure reaches 0 or less SHP, it collapses in 1d10 rounds.
Rule of thumb: 1 SHP per ton of weight.
Man-sized weapons and light ballista cannot damage wooden structures.
Huge creatures and magic deal only 1/5 damage to wooden structures.
Artillery heavier than light ballista, and gigantic or larger creatures, deal normal damage to wooden structures.
Wood-throwing artillery and huge creatures cannot damage stone or earthen structures.
Stone-throwing artillery and gigantic creatures deal only 1/10 damage to stone structures.
Colossal creatures and magic deal only 1/5 damage to stone structures.
Petards deal normal damage to stone structures.
Unit capacity is the number of company-sized units a fortified structure can garrison.

item.name: Arrow Slit
item.rule: Missile attacks against creatures behind arrow slits suffer -4.
Defenders gain +4 to saves vs Blast from artillery, burning oil, or similar effects.
On a successful save, protected creatures take no damage even when the effect would normally deal half.
Standard density is 1 arrow slit per 5' of wall.

item.name: Barbican
item.rule: Consists of a gatehouse, two small towers, and a drawbridge.
May sit outside the stronghold and connect to the walls by a short neck.

item.name: Battlement
item.rule: Missile attacks against protected defenders suffer -4.
Protected defenders gain +4 to saves vs Blast from artillery, burning oil, or similar effects.
On a successful save, protected creatures take no damage even when the effect would normally deal half.

item.name: Building
item.rule: Standard fortified building is 20' high and 30' square, with wooden doors, floors, roof, and stairs.
Its walls are thicker than comparable civilian structures, resulting in higher SHP.
Variant dimensions adjust price and SHP proportionately.

item.name: Drawbridge
item.rule: Standard drawbridge is 10' wide, 20' high, and 1' thick.
Variant dimensions adjust price and SHP proportionately.

item.name: Gatehouse
item.rule: Standard gatehouse is 20' high, 30' wide, 20' long, with 10' thick walls and a metal portcullis.
Variant dimensions adjust price and SHP proportionately.

item.name: Keep
item.rule: Standard keep is 80' high and 60' square with 10' thick stone walls.
Interior has wooden doors and stairs between 8 floors.
Variant square keeps adjust price and SHP proportionately.
Round keeps cost 50% more and gain +1 AC.

item.name: Moat
item.rule: Standard moat is 100' long, 20' wide, 10' deep.
Variant dimensions adjust price proportionately.
Moats do not have SHP.
Moats may be filled with fascines.

item.name: Palisade
item.rule: Standard palisade is 10' high, 100' long, 1' thick.
Variant dimensions adjust price and SHP proportionately.
A 100' palisade can be defended by 1 unit.

item.name: Rampart
item.rule: Standard rampart is 10' high, 100' long, 15' thick.
Variant dimensions adjust price and SHP proportionately.
A 100' rampart can be defended by 1 unit.
Earthworks such as mottes and siege ramps use this construction method.

item.name: Tower
item.rule: Towers have 5' thick round walls, wooden doors, floors, and stairs.
They have 1 story per 10' of height.
Variant round towers adjust price and SHP proportionately.
Square towers cost 50% less but lose 1 AC.
Small and medium towers hold 1 unit; large towers hold 2; huge towers hold 5.

item.name: Wall
item.rule: Standard stone wall is 100' long and 10' thick, with normal listed heights of 20'-60'.
Variant dimensions adjust price and SHP proportionately.
Walls may be built up to 200' high.
Construction over 60' high doubles cost.
A 100' wall can be defended by 1.5 units on top of the wall, plus an additional 1.5 units per 10' of height firing through arrow slits.
For multi-story arrow defense, 1 arrow slit per 5' per story is required.
Add the length of all wall sections together to determine total defending capacity.

overview.rule: Construction is handled as construction projects.
Default project type is stronghold construction.
Other project types include shipbuilding, siege engine manufacture, field fortification, ammunition scavenging, and sapping.

construction_cost_rate_and_supervision.rule: Construction cost equals the base cost of the project in gp.
Each worker contributes a construction rate in gp value per day toward the construction cost.
A worker's construction rate is normally identical to the worker's wage rate.
Optional simplification: every laborer may be treated as having a construction rate of 1 2/3 sp per day, so 3,000 laborers construct 500gp per day.
Unskilled laborers have wage and construction rate of 3gp/month or 1sp/day.
Skilled laborers have wage and construction rate of 6gp/month or 2sp/day.
About 1 in 4 laborers is usually a skilled laborer.
A master craftsman may manage up to 2 journeymen and 4 apprentices to increase their construction rate by 50%.
On a large-scale construction project taking more than a day, a master craftsman managing junior craftsmen reduces the master's own personal construction rate by 25%.
Usually there is no more than 1 master craftsman per 100 laborers.
A siege engineer works at a journeyman craftsman construction rate.
An engineer works at a master craftsman construction rate.
Characters with only 1 rank of Siege Engineering count as skilled laborers, not siege engineers.
Monstrous workers multiply normal unskilled laborer construction rate by normal load divided by 5, rounded down.
Every project requires a construction supervisor.
A siege engineer may supervise 1 project up to 25,000gp construction cost.
An engineer may supervise 1 project up to 100,000gp construction cost.
Multiple engineers or siege engineers may combine to supervise larger projects.

wage_notes.rule: Troops on labor detail must still be paid their normal wage rate.
Slaves or prisoners need not be paid wages.

construction_sites.rule: A construction site is the geographic area around a project, generally about 1/2 mile in diameter.
All similar construction at the same site must be consolidated into one construction project.
A maximum of 12,000 workers may work on one site.
The first 3,000 workers operate at full construction rate.
Any additional workers beyond 3,000 operate at only 33% of normal construction rate, but still draw full wages.
Using more than 3,000 workers therefore increases wage cost above the base labor cost while reducing total construction time.

construction_materials.rule: Nearby forests and quarries are assumed; local raw material gathering is already included in labor cost.
If raw materials must be transported from long distance, increase labor cost by 10%, 20%, or more.
Buying raw materials at market costs 25% of total project cost and reduces labor cost by 25%.
Scavenging raw materials from nearby buildings reduces labor cost by 25%, but reduces the buildings' value by twice that amount.

assisting_construction_with_magic.rule: A spellcaster with Engineering proficiency, or working under an engineer, may assist construction with magic.
Move earth applies only to ditches, moats, and earthen ramparts.
Move earth gives a construction rate of 12,500gp per turn for those projects, for 6 turns, for 75,000gp total per casting.
Transmute rock to mud increases workers' construction rate by 50% for the spell duration of 3d6 days by allowing stone to be worked as earth.
Using transmute rock to mud plus move earth to pour transformed mud into wooden molds lets workers construct stone structures as if wooden, doubling workers' construction rate.
Using wall of stone to create molds for the transformed mud adds 500gp of construction per wall of stone casting.
Wall of stone may also resurface existing stone at 5,000gp of stronghold value per casting.
Wall of stone may instantly and permanently erect a stone structure of up to 250gp value.
Such wall of stone structures are critically weak to dispel magic; any dispel magic functions as disintegrate against them.

artillery_and_siege_equipment_constructi.rule: Constructing artillery or siege equipment is handled as a construction project.
Normal construction-site limits do not apply; any number of siege engines may be constructed simultaneously at the same site if enough supervisors are available.
Huge siege towers are capped at 1,200 workers.
Large siege towers are capped at 300 workers.
All other artillery and siege equipment are capped at 50 workers.
Because of these worker caps, craftsmen usually do most of the work.

ship_construction.rule: Building a ship is handled as a construction project.
The construction site must be adjacent to a navigable waterway.
Normal construction-site limits do not apply; any number of ships may be built simultaneously at the same site if enough supervisors are available.
The number of workers able to work on a ship equals the ship's maximum crew.
